newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee seminar sees international interest.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee seminar sees international interest.

text.p: Representatives from coffee sectors in Colombia, the Ivory Coast, Germany, Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, the U.S. and the U.K. will attend a Brazilian seminar being held January 20-22, the organisers said.

The conference will open in Rio de Janeiro on the afternoon of January 20 with a panel discussing the importance of coffee to the Brazilian government as well as a new council to be installed tomorrow which will decide Brazilian coffee policy.

The conference is the first to be held in Brazil for the past nine years. However the government has already said that it would like to hold a similar event in the second half of 1998, said Francisco Ourique, one of the event's organisers.
In the afternoon of January 21, the president of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) Rubens Barbosa will speak on the role of the association in the expansion of world consumption.

He will be joined by Robert Nelson of the U.S. National Coffee Association who will discuss the coffee consumption outlook for the U.S while Germany's Frieder Rotzoll will look at the same subject from the European perspective.
In the morning of the same day, a variety of speakers will address the prospects for the Brazilian 1997/98 crop as well as domestic consumption.

The first speaker in this session is scheduled to be Leon Yallouz, formerly the U.S. Department of Agriculture's representative in Rio de Janeiro and who is now carrying out crop forecasts as a private consultant.
Yallouz has already sent out his first report to clients but will not be issuing any actual estimate at the conference.
"Many people who have been following my work for so many years have no idea about what actually I do. So I will be talking a little about what I do, when I do it and how I do it," Yallouz said.
Yallouz said he will also speak about his last field trip in October and the vegetative state of the trees at that time as well as looking at future production potential in Brazil.
The head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation Jorge Cardenas will on the afternoon of January 22 speak on price perspectives.
He will be joined by ACPC secretary-general Roberio da Silva who will give a speech on price stabilisation and systems of commercialisation.

The seminar will be followed by an emergency meeting of ACPC members on January 23. The council was called after African nations, backed by Colombia, expressed the need for exports between January and June this year to be cut further.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
